arxiv-2102-04297.description: Abstract The empirical success of deep learning is often attributed to SGD’s mysterious ability to avoid sharp local minima in the loss landscape, as sharp minima are known to lead to poor generalization. Recently, evidence of heavy-tailed gradient noise was reported in many deep learning tasks, and it was shown in ( Şimşekli et al. 2019a ; Şimşekli et al.

arxiv-2105-04265.description: Abstract Let ξ 1 , ξ 2 , … \xi_{1},\xi_{2},\dots be i.i.d. non-negative random variables whose tail varies regularly with index − 1 -1 , let S n S_{n} be the sum and M n M_{n} the largest of the first n n values.

arxiv-2205-08204.title: Three-Dirac-fermion approach to unexpected universal gapless surface states in van der Waals magnetic topological insulators
arxiv-2205-08204.creator: Dinghui Wang 1 , Huaiqiang Wang 1,∗ , Dingyu Xing 1,2 , and Haijun Zhang 1,2,∗
arxiv-2205-08204.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Dinghui Wang 1 , Huaiqiang Wang 1,∗ , Dingyu Xing 1,2 , and Haijun Zhang 1,2,∗. Layered van der Waals (vdW) topological materials, especially the recently discovered MnBi 2 Te 4 -family magnetic topological insulators (TIs), have aroused great attention. However, there has been a serious debate about whether the surface states are gapped or gapless for antiferromagnetic (AFM) TI MnBi 2 Te 4 , which is crucial to the prospect of various magnetic topological phenomena.

arxiv-2211-09864.creator: Kyle Deeds, Dan Suciu, Magda Balazinska
arxiv-2211-09864.description: Abstract . Recent work has reemphasized the importance of cardinality estimates for query optimization. While new techniques have continuously improved in accuracy over time, they still generally allow for under-estimates which often lead optimizers to make overly optimistic decisions. This can be very costly for expensive queries.

arxiv-2303-16576.title: WordStylist: Styled Verbatim Handwritten Text Generation with Latent Diffusion Models
arxiv-2303-16576.creator: Konstantina Nikolaidou, George Retsinas, Vincent Christlein, Mathias Seuret, Giorgos Sfikas, Elisa Barney Smith, Hamam Mokayed, Marcus Liwicki
arxiv-2303-16576.description: Abstract Text-to-Image synthesis is the task of generating an image according to a specific text description. Generative Adversarial Networks have been considered the standard method for image synthesis virtually since their introduction. Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models are recently setting a new baseline, with remarkable results in Text-to-Image synthesis, among other fields.

arxiv-2502-06022.title: Nested subspace learning with flags
arxiv-2502-06022.creator: Tom Szwagiertom.szwagier@inria.fr, Xavier Pennec xavier.pennec@inria.fr
arxiv-2502-06022.description: Abstract Many machine learning methods look for low-dimensional representations of the data. The underlying subspace can be estimated by first choosing a dimension q q and then optimizing a certain objective function over the space of q q -dimensional subspaces—the Grassmannian.

arxiv-2502-11992.title: On the Logic Elements Associated with Round-Off Errors and Gaussian Blur in Image Registration: A Simple Case of Commingling
arxiv-2502-11992.creator: Serap A. Savari
arxiv-2502-11992.description: Abstract Discrete image registration can be a strategy to reconstruct signals from samples corrupted by blur and noise. We examine superresolution and discrete image registration for one-dimensional spatially-limited piecewise constant functions which are subject to blur which is Gaussian or a mixture of Gaussians as well as to round-off errors.

arxiv-2503-03943.title: Bubbles-induced transition to elasto-inertial turbulence
arxiv-2503-03943.creator: Hafiz Usman Naseer 1, Daulet Izbassarov 2, Marco Edoardo Rosti 3, Metin Muradoglu 1
arxiv-2503-03943.description: Abstract Interface-resolved direct numerical simulations are performed to investigate bubble-induced transition from laminar to elasto-inertial turbulent (EIT) state in a pressure-driven viscoelastic square channel flow. The Giesekus model is used to account for the viscoelasticity of the continuous phase while the dispersed phase is Newtonian.

arxiv-2505-16594.title: Temporal Object Captioning for Street Scene Videos from LiDAR Tracks Thanks: Identify applicable funding agency here. If none, delete this.
arxiv-2505-16594.creator: 1 st Vignesh Gopinathan, 2 nd Urs Zimmermann, 3 rd Michael Arnold, 4 th Matthias Rottmann
arxiv-2505-16594.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by 1 st Vignesh Gopinathan, 2 nd Urs Zimmermann, 3 rd Michael Arnold, 4 th Matthias Rottmann. Video captioning models have seen notable advancements in recent years, especially with regard to their ability to capture temporal information. While many research efforts have focused on architectural advancements, such as temporal attention mechanisms, there remains a notable gap in understanding how models capture and utilize temporal semantics for effective temporal feature extraction, especially in the context of Advanced Driver Assistance Systems.

arxiv-2508-00130.title: Computation of Approximately Stable Committees in Approval-based Elections
arxiv-2508-00130.creator: Drew Gao, Yihang Sun, Jan Vondrák
arxiv-2508-00130.description: Abstract Approval-based committee selection is a model of significant interest in social choice theory. In this model, we have a set of voters 𝒱 {\mathcal{V}} , a set of candidates 𝒞 {\mathcal{C}} , and each voter has a set A v ⊂ 𝒞 A_{v}\subset{\mathcal{C}} of approved candidates.

arxiv-2601-00297.title: Generalized 2 2 -split for higher-derivative YM and GR amplitudes at tree-level
arxiv-2601-00297.creator: Liang Zhang, Kang Zhou
arxiv-2601-00297.description: Abstract We study the generalized 2 2 -split of higher-derivative amplitudes, including Yang-Mills (YM) and Gravity (GR) amplitudes with special insertions of higher-derivative vertices, by expanding them into YM ⊕ BAS {\rm YM}\oplus{\rm BAS} , GR ⊕ YM {\rm GR}\oplus{\rm YM} , and GR ⊕ YM ⊕ BAS {\rm GR}\oplus{\rm YM}\oplus{\rm BAS} amplitude, respectively.

pmc-10514047.title: Thermodynamic forces from protein and water govern condensate formation of an intrinsically disordered protein domain
pmc-10514047.creator: Saumyak Mukherjee, Lars V Schäfer
pmc-10514047.description: Liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) can drive a multitude of cellular processes by compartmentalizing biological cells via the formation of dense liquid biomolecular condensates, which can function as membraneless organelles. Despite its importance, the molecular-level understanding of the underlying thermodynamics of this process remains incomplete.

pmc-11423205.title: Case report: Improvement of gait with adaptive deep brain stimulation in a patient with Parkinson’s disease
pmc-11423205.creator: Ioannis U. Isaias, Laura Caffi, Linda Borellini, Antonella M. Ampollini, Marco Locatelli, Gianni Pezzoli, Alberto Mazzoni, Chiara Palmisano
pmc-11423205.description: Gait disturbance is a common and severe symptom of Parkinson’s disease that severely impairs quality of life. Current treatments provide only partial benefits with wide variability in outcomes. Also, deep brain stimulation of the subthalamic nucleus (STN-DBS), a mainstay treatment for bradykinetic-rigid symptoms and parkinsonian tremor, is poorly effective on gait.

pmc-11625766.title: Integrating multi-omics techniques and in vitro experiments reveals that GLRX3 regulates the immune microenvironment and promotes hepatocellular carcinoma cell proliferation and invasion through iron metabolism pathways
pmc-11625766.creator: Yang Li, Yuan Chen, Yang Zhang, Yunsheng Fang, Ling Wu, Ying Zhao, Danqiong Wang, Xiaoyuan Qiao
pmc-11625766.description: BackgroundHepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a common malignancy worldwide, and its development is closely related to abnormalities in iron metabolism. This study aims to systematically analyze changes in iron metabolism in the tumor microenvironment of HCC using single-cell sequencing technology, and investigate the potential mechanisms by which iron metabolism regulation affects the survival of liver cancer patients.

pmc-12595309.title: Molecular mechanisms and biomarkers of total parenteral nutrition-induced hepatotoxicity revealed by iTRAQ proteomics analysis
pmc-12595309.creator: Yung-Yu Hsieh, Jai-Jen Tsai, Shui-Yi Tung, Ko-Chao Lee, Kung-Chuan Cheng, Kam-Fai Lee, Meng-Chiao Hsieh, Cheng-Yi Huang, Chih-Chuan Teng, Chien-Heng Shen, Hsing-Chun Kuo
pmc-12595309.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background/Aims: Total parenteral nutrition (TPN) provides medical nutrients intravenously to patients who cannot obtain proper nutrition through normal dietary means or enteral feeding. One significant concern is the risk of liver damage associated with long-term TPN use. In this study, the TPN-associated acute liver injury proteins and the molecular mechanisms underlying TPN oxidative stress were investigated through a quantitative proteomic survey.

pmc-13092690.title: Blood-based biomarker discovery for early pregnancy loss using integrative multi-omics strategies
pmc-13092690.creator: Yue Shi, Yongkang Yang, Xianghao Guo, Shuai Shi, Qin Li, Chi Chiu Wang, Liona C Poon, Pui Wah Chung, Jianan Xia, Yongfei Wang, Xingqiang Lai, Yueqiong Ni, Xiaoyan Chen, Yao Wang
pmc-13092690.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryBackgroundEarly pregnancy loss (EPL), a spontaneous death of the embryo or foetus occurring within the first trimester, is a major challenge for human reproduction with profound adverse consequences for women's health. Currently, reliable blood-based biomarkers for EPL remain limited. Therefore, there is an urgent need to discover novel biomarkers for EPL using a multi-omics-based approach to facilitate early detection and timely management.MethodsIn the discovery cohort, 40 patients with EPL and 40 healthy pregnancies (HP) at 7–13 weeks of gestation were enrolled.

pmc-13093002.title: Developmental assets and mental health among black sexual minority male adolescents: A dominance analysis of depressive symptoms and suicidal behaviors
pmc-13093002.creator: Donte T. Boyd, Hans Oh, Akilah Patterson, Addie Weaver, Myles Durkee, Camille R. Quinn
pmc-13093002.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study examined associations between developmental assets and mental health outcomes among Black sexual minority male (BSMM) adolescents aged 14–17 in the Midwestern United States. Data were collected through an online survey of 383 participants. Dominance analysis was employed to evaluate the relative contributions of multiple developmental assets, including positive identity, social competencies, family support, positive values, and mattering and belonging, as well as depressive symptoms and suicidal behaviors.

pmc-13150673.title: Real‐World Outcomes of Baricitinib and Ritlecitinib in Refractory Alopecia Areata: Response Predictors and Relapse After Discontinuation or Dose Reduction
pmc-13150673.creator: Rina Hayashi, Saori Takamura, Tomoo Fukuda
pmc-13150673.description: Baricitinib and ritlecitinib are newly approved systemic Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitors for severe, refractory alopecia areata (AA). Although clinical trials have demonstrated their efficacy, real‐world evidence remains limited, particularly regarding predictors of response and outcomes following treatment interruption or dose tapering.

pmc-13301471.title: Catheter ablation of idiopathic premature ventricular contractions in athletes without structural heart disease: impact on arrhythmic burden and return to sport
pmc-13301471.creator: F Cardinali, Y Valeri, R Grandin, G Giacomini, G Castellucci, L D'angelo, F Campanelli, L Finori, L Sabatelli, G Volpato, P Compagnucci, L Cipolletta, Q Parisi, M Casella, A Dello Russo
pmc-13301471.description: BackgroundPremature ventricular contractions (PVCs) are frequently observed in athletes and are usually idiopathic and benign, most commonly arising from the right or left ventricular outflow tract (RVOT/LVOT) or fascicular system. However, the management of symptomatic or high-burden PVCs in athletes remains controversial, especially regarding eligibility and timing of return to sport after catheter ablation (CA).

pmc-13315126.title: Fifty Years From the First Framingham Risk Profile: Are We Getting Closer to Identifying and PREVENTing Subclinical Disease Progression?
pmc-13315126.creator: Catherine G Derington, Larry A Allen
pmc-13315126.description: nt of imaging modalities that better identify and characterize the spectrum of cardiovascular disease combined with a proliferation of biomarkers and more sophisticated prediction algorithms, cardiovascular risk scores have continued to evolve. The next era of cardiovascular prevention is being pushed to ask how well risk scores predict subclinical disease and what do we do with that information.

pmc-13625481.title: Longitudinal changes in vessel density and retinal nerve fiber layer thickness after acute primary angle closure
pmc-13625481.creator: Qian Hao, Yuan Qin, Linwei Yan, Yue Wang, Ju Li, Fang Fan
pmc-13625481.description: ObjectiveTo evaluate the initial and longitudinal alterations of peripapillary optic disc vessel index in eyes with a history of acute primary angle closure (APAC) and to explore the better predictor of glaucoma progression.MethodsTwenty-one consecutive Chinese patients who were successfully treated for a unilateral episode of APAC were included in the study.
